# R72: Persistent identity-aware phase classes and complete interval membership

Author-side mathematical report, 2026-11-11. Predecessor R71: `0b5319d7a0caf90dcd210e291152c6c06bbc2828`. Scientific S23/AV frozen input: `43ec6098b1330ae86d0a7863be336c5d97f6ef34` (unchanged). This is an **auxiliary rational circular-source model**, not a native X6/BRC theorem, Task CLAIM, Result or Review.

## Domain
Finite collection E of independent (integer time t, branch-ID) sources. Reduced rational anchor theta0=p/q (q>0), rational phase x, integer observer time j, parameter I=[L,U] containing theta0, and integer original boundary labels a,b. Assume the endpoint floors k_a=floor(a L)=floor(a U), k_b=floor(b L)=floor(b U) are constant; the affine nonwrapping target arc A(theta)=a theta-k_a < B(theta)=b theta-k_b holds at both endpoints (hence throughout I). Target membership is `{x+(t-j)theta} in [A(theta),B(theta))`. The upper endpoint is excluded.

## Theorem 1: identity-preserving persistent grouping
Index all event identities by residue r=(t p mod q). Use a persistent ordered map of nonempty residues; each value is a persistent ordered multiset of independently keyed (t,branch) identities, with exact subtree min-time, max-time and count. Insertion/deletion reconstructs only the affected inner path and outer path; if the inner set becomes empty remove the residue. Each immutable version enumerates exactly its source identities and every class extremum/count matches that version. Deleting one of two branches at a shared time does not remove the other.

*Proof:* Induct on updates. An inner update changes precisely one identity and recomputes aggregate min/max/count from its own key and child aggregates. Immutable unaffected nodes are reused. The outer path replaces only this class root or deletes an empty class. Existing roots are immutable, hence their identity set and all summaries remain unchanged. The code's deterministic 128-bit pseudo-priorities do **not** imply a deterministic logarithmic complexity bound. For genuinely independent randomized treap priorities and an update sequence independent of them, classical expected search/path-copy costs are O(log(g+1)+log(n_r+1)), where g is the class count and n_r the affected class size.

## Theorem 2: complete integer-level existential membership
For a source e let alpha(theta)=x+(t-j)theta, D_B=alpha-B, and D_A=alpha-A. The exact membership equivalence is

    {alpha(theta)} in [A(theta),B(theta))
    <=> exists integer k: D_B(theta) < k <= D_A(theta).

Because both D functions are affine, any possible integer k lies in the finite set

    k = floor(min_{theta in I} D_B)+1, ... , floor(max_{theta in I} D_A).

For each k, solve the two one-dimensional rational affine constraints

    alpha(theta)-A(theta)-k >= 0,
    alpha(theta)-B(theta)-k < 0

inside I, tracking open/closed bounds. If any intersection is nonempty, it has a **rational witness** (a closed singleton or rational midpoint); otherwise the event is OUT for every real theta in I. This proves soundness and completeness on the stated stable nonwrapping arc, including integer source-phase wraps and one-point boundary contacts, without enumerating source-floor jump points.

*Proof:* Choose the integer lift of the source fractional phase. The half-open arc condition rearranges to the displayed inequalities. Endpoint extrema bound every admissible k because D_A, D_B are affine. The rational half-line intersection is exact. Nonempty rational intervals with rational endpoints always contain rational witnesses. Both directions hold for all real parameters.

## Theorem 3: complete two-valued hybrid
Use R71's sufficient closed-envelope integer-shift exclusion for the entire source collection. On failure and small class count g, apply it to each exact anchor-phase class. Then run the complete Theorem-2 checker only for events in the unresolved classes; for g above a resource threshold go directly to per-event exact checking. The output is exactly one of:

- ALL_OUT: for all real theta in I, all events are excluded.
- EXISTS_MEMBER: one explicitly identified (t,branch) and rational theta witness.

*Proof:* Sound sufficient exclusions never discard a possibly present source. Every unpruned source is decided by the complete Theorem-2 oracle. Thus the disjunction over all source existences is exactly computed. Failure of any sufficient envelope is UNKNOWN for that envelope alone, not a negative result.

**Certificate cache:** An exclusion certificate applies across later persistent versions only when the *identical immutable inner class-root object* is reused, (theta0,j,x,a,b) are identical, and the new query I' is contained in the certified I. Immutable structural identity fixes all class identities, and universal quantification restricts to subintervals. A changed class, anchor, observer, original boundary labels, or noncontained interval requires recalculation. Store strong references to cached roots, not only recycled runtime object IDs.

**Cost scope:** class construction stores O(n) source identities plus O(g) map keys; updates path-copy actual treap traversals. For an individual source the finite integer-level fallback visits K_e= max(0, floor(max D_A)-floor(min D_B)) integers, which may be large for broad intervals and large time. Full integer bit costs and memory accounting are not discharged. The full local checker implements two-level persistent treaps; the repository's mini checker is an independent concise semantic reproduction and uses immutable sorted versions instead of the treap stress harness.

## Executed exact evidence
Full local `check_r72.py` with Python Fraction and seed 7220261111: 11,520 insert/delete consistency checks, 2,700 historical-version readbacks, 890 exact hybrid-vs-direct whole-interval query comparisons, 150 independent finite-critical-stratum whole-interval oracle comparisons examining 572 strata, and 2,670 pointwise checks. Targeted cases include the R70 wrap witness with time 6, the R71 two-phase family, distinct branches at one time, deletions of extrema, the {1,9} vs {1,5,9} four-extrema witness, and lower-included/upper-excluded singleton intervals. All assertions passed. The smaller `check_r72_min.py` also executed with `R72_MIN_PASS 65 ...`.

In one unreplicated local Python timing run on the two-phase family (n=32/128/512/1024), persistent index construction cost 0.000493/0.001935/0.009187/0.019914 s, 20 matched complete queries cost 0.001996/0.001982/0.002131/0.002750 s hybrid vs 0.014057/0.059530/0.219468/0.449537 s direct. This favorable family is not a universal speedup or bit-cost benchmark. On 890 random parameter queries the hybrid chose 110 class-refinement and 780 direct fallbacks (group budget 4). Independent mathematical review pending.

## Next R73
Adapt R66/R68 comparators to **the same complete all-real decision obligation**, rather than comparing a sufficient UNKNOWN result with a complete query. Quantify integer-bit operations, heap/persistent-node memory, crossover of update- and read-heavy workloads, maintain global extrema without scanning all groups, and extend to latest-source with branch-tie semantics. Treat arcs crossing zero by an explicit separate piecewise specification. Preserve unchanged S23/AV pin and P000.
